materials.provenance: Base colour re-baked (Cycles CPU, emission, selected-to-active) from the approved TRELLIS source mesh onto fresh smart-projected UVs (the source atlas does not survive the cut and decimation) after the reconstructed wheels were cut away; no rear-view projection (the far side, underside and the canopy's open rear end are as TRELLIS invented them). Tangent normals baked from the source geometry and whiteout-blended with colour relief; AO baked from the decimated geometry; roughness and metalness derived from colour inside declared regions (pale canvas above 1.05 m; dark, unsaturated iron fittings). Base colour lifted by luma power toneGamma (chroma ratios kept), set by eye, not calibrated against the concept. Base alpha opaque (never dyed). Artistic derivation, not measured PBR.

baseEncoding.reason: Base-colour alpha is the dye mask; libwebp's default lossy mode discards RGB under alpha 0.

settings.POSITION: SHORT normalized; one uniform scale per mesh folded into its node's scale (no offset), the inverse into its children
settings.TEXCOORD: UNSIGNED_SHORT normalized where the UVs lie in [0, 1]

reorder.method: meshoptimizer reorderMesh: vertex-cache triangle order, then vertex-fetch vertex order
reorder.check: a permutation: every vertex keeps its exact attribute bytes, and the triangles are the same, with the same winding, in another order

geometryCompression.check: every view decoded again: attribute views byte-identical to the reordered data; triangle index views hold the same triangles in the same order and winding (only the first vertex may rotate)

derivedFrom.note: The exact real-004-q output, reordered for locality and compressed by meshopt_glb.mjs (EXT_meshopt_compression, no lossy filters); the Blender cook was not re-run.

cook.scriptsNote: SHA-256 of each script with LF line endings, equal to its copy in scripts/models/pipeline.
cook.verification: tests/wagon-models.test.ts checks the body, one spun node per axle whose rim touches the ground, the harness tips within 6 cm of the draft ox's hame hooks, the budgets, WebP maps and normals, and drives the wagon through the presenter without a DOM; tests/wagons-browser.test.ts decodes and renders it in the game's WebGL presenter.

limitations: Single-view TRELLIS reconstruction from one approved concept: the far side, back and underside are TRELLIS's invention, with no rear-view painting projected onto them.
Roughness, metalness and ambient occlusion are derived from colour inside declared regions and Cycles bakes, not measured PBR or hand-painted masks.
One body mesh with its detail painted into a single 1024 px base colour; there are no LODs, trim sheets or separate material layers.
The base colour is lifted by luma power 0.85 (chroma kept), set by eye in review renders, not calibrated against the concept.
Re-cooking is not guaranteed to be byte-reproducible: MikkTSpace tangents can round differently on a few vertices, and Blender's smart UV project can lay out an atlas differently between runs.

The reconstructed wheels, drawbar and ground clutter were cut away and replaced by Blender-authored spoked wheels (1,972 triangles per axle node), shafts, crossbar, duga arch, warding bell and pennant with procedural wood grain: clean and sharper than the reconstructed body, and visibly a different kind of surface up close.

The TRELLIS texture atlas does not survive the cut and decimation (the first cooks showed smeared, streaked base colour), so the body is unwrapped afresh (smart UV project) and its base colour re-baked from the source mesh: detail is TRELLIS's 2048 px reconstruction resampled to 1024 px.
The wooden parts' paint was sampled from the concept by eye; wheels and shafts are darker than the first cooks, which read far too light in game.
The pennant is a static rippled cloth (enlarged and rippled after the in-game review so it still reads from straight behind); it does not flutter, and the canvas and ropes do not move.
The body and wheels lean 0.085 rad about the centreline when disabled, as the procedural wagon did, so one rim lifts and the other sinks by up to about 8 cm.
The canvas cover and the bed are one reconstructed surface with the TRELLIS-invented open rear end of the canopy; the hanging bucket and ropes are fused lumps up close.
The pennant takes the faction colour; the procedural convoy's flag was always teal.
